purpose: Piroxicam is used to relieve pain, swelling, and stiffness caused by arthritis, including osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis. It helps you move more comfortably and go about your daily activities with less discomfort. It is a long-acting anti-inflammatory medicine, so you only need to take it once a day.
how_it_works: Your body makes certain chemicals called prostaglandins that cause pain, swelling, and inflammation. Piroxicam works by blocking the enzymes (called COX-1 and COX-2) that your body uses to make those chemicals. With fewer of those chemicals around, you feel less pain and your joints are less swollen and stiff.
common_side_effects: Upset stomach, nausea, heartburn, or indigestion are the most common side effects. Some people notice stomach pain, diarrhea, or constipation. Dizziness, headache, or mild swelling in the hands and feet can also occur. Taking it with food or milk can help reduce stomach upset.
warnings: This medicine can increase the risk of serious stomach bleeding or ulcers, especially if you are older, drink alcohol, or take blood thinners. It may also raise the risk of heart attack or stroke, so it should be used at the lowest effective dose for the shortest time needed. Do not take it if you are allergic to aspirin or other NSAIDs. Always tell your doctor if you have kidney, liver, or heart problems before taking this medication.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 20 mg taken once a day by mouth, with food or milk to protect your stomach. Your doctor may sometimes split this into two 10 mg doses per day. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and do not take more than prescribed.
